# `streaming_event_content_exists`

> Every playback event refers to catalog content (royalties are paid per content item).

| | |
|---|---|
| Domain | [streaming](README.md) |
| Layer | **silver** — evaluated by the `silver` gate |
| Model | `slv_streaming__playback_events` (`streaming_silver.slv_streaming__playback_events`) |
| Column | `content_id` |
| Check | `relationships` |
| Severity | `error` — a violation **stops the pipeline** |
| Defined in | [dbt/models/streaming/silver/_silver.yml](../../../dbt/models/streaming/silver/_silver.yml) |

## What it checks

Every `content_id` exists as `content_id` in `slv_streaming__content`.

## When it fails

The `silver` task of `medallion_streaming` fails, gold and `publish_gold` don't run, and the batch is never added to `streaming_gold`: consumers keep the batches published before. `quality_report` marks the run as blocked and sends the alert, if one is configured.

The rows that broke the rule in its latest evaluation are kept in `dq_audit.streaming_event_content_exists`.

## Tested by

Scenario **`unknown_content`**: events for content not in the catalog.

```bash
make generate DOMAIN=streaming SCENARIO=unknown_content BATCH=2026-10-20_unknown_content
make pipeline DOMAIN=streaming BATCH=2026-10-20_unknown_content
```

## Investigate

```sql

select * from dq_audit.streaming_event_content_exists;

-- history of the rule
select batch_id, status, failures, recorded_at
from dq_audit.rule_results
where rule = 'streaming_event_content_exists'
order by recorded_at desc;
```
